utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Unfortunately, today Judge Van den Wyngaert is unable to sit. We expect that she will be able to sit tomorrow. We will continue under Rule 15 bis today. We understand that it would be preferable, given the condition of the witness, if we had only one hour sessions rather than the normal longer session to enable her to have some movement. That being so, I mention it now so that particularly Ms. Residovic can be aware that we will break after approximately an hour. If I could remind the witness that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Ms. Groseva. My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I appear on behalf Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Ms. Groseva, before I start asking you questions that I have planned for you, I suppose that you understand the language that I'm speaking and I also understand your language. However, my question needs to be interpreted so that the Chamber and the other colleagues in the courtroom are able to hear what I'm asking you and hear your answers, so I'm asking you to start answering only when my question is already interpreted. There is the way that we are of best assistance to the Chamber. Have you understood this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please answer it, because it needs to be recorded in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you stated that you were born in Skopje and that you live there. You have lived there for all your life. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Skopje, you graduated from the faculty of law. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1992 until the present day you are an employee of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, if I say that from the beginning of your professional life you were employed in the republic Ministry of the Internal Affairs and not in a department or a sector at the level of a municipality or the city, that would also be correct. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You held a different offices in the ministry. You first worked as analyst in the sector for analytics and research. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you were the head analyst for public law and order within that same sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only in 2002 you worked as a senior advisor for the normative activities in the legal sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again, from 1st of January, 2003, you were transferred to the sector of analytics and you are the head of the department for analysis and information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today you hold the office of the head of the entire sector, and apart from the department for analysis and information there is also a department for statistical researches and analysis. Is that information correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So during the events at Ljuboten, in August 2001, you were the head analyst for public law and order within the sector for analysis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the time when the minister Hari Kostov appointed you a member of the committee that you discussed yesterday with my learned colleague the Prosecutor, you were the head of the department for analysis and information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had the capacity of an authorised official in all these posts, all these offices that you held from beginning of your employment at the ministry until the present day?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, the law on internal affairs stipulates who are the officers in the ministry who hold the status of authorised official. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to that law, the authorised officials are primarily members of the police and the operational officers, then officers who are directly linked to the police and the operational officers, the minister, minister's deputies, and other managerial staff. Would this be a brief summary of what the law stipulates as authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, although you were an authorised official for the entire duration of your employment that does not mean that at all that you were able to perform any -- just any duty that the Ministry of the Interior carries out?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, your tasks and the scope of the tasks were set forth in the Rule Book of Organisation of the Ministry of Interior. Would that conclusion be correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That same rule book sets forth the scope of work for the sector of analytics where you actually spent most of your career. And this act also stipulates that your sector performs the analytics, research and information tasks; maintains the information and statistical evidence; produces analysis, reviews information and other materials; follows, studies and analyses the security situation according to the data coming from the public security; proposals are tabled for certain actions that need to be carried within the ministry; the law enforcement is followed and also other tasks are performed as stipulated by the law. Would this be a summary of the tasks as stipulated in the Rule book and as you really carry out actually in your work?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Ms. Groseva, that the sector for analytics, exists also in another part of the Ministry of Interior within the state security, and that sector performs the same or similar tasks as your sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that such sector exists in the security and counter-intelligence directorate, but whether these type of tasks are carried out there, I could not say, since we do not cooperate with that sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. But you surely know that their scope of work is also regulated by a general act on the operation of the officers of the security and counter-intelligence directorate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, you had already nine years of working experience from the moment that you started working at the ministry and at the moment you were appointed as a member of the committee that the minister Hari Kostov established, you had 11 years of working experience and you had actual experience working in the analytics. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you stated just a moment ago, you were an authorised official but you were not able to carry out just any task of the Ministry of Interior. Thus, you could not perform the tasks of the operational officers and you were not authorised as the operational officers in the operative department to take statements that they are able to take in the pre-trial procedure pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, you could not go out to the street as an authorised official and regulate the traffic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I repeat from what you stated before, the scope of work, the duties and responsibilities were regulated with the general act of organisation and operations of the Ministry of the Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the law and the general act, you also carried out the operations in accordance with the orders given by your immediate superior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were just an analyst in the sector, you received order from the head of the analytics department, and later from the head of the sector, and now you receive orders from the director of public security bureau. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering what you stated now, the tasks, the operational work are regulated by acts. Is it correct, Ms. Groseva, that in the same way the issue of responsibility of officers is regulated, and that that responsibility is also set forth in the general acts of the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Firstly, the officer is accountable to his or her immediate superior who performs the actual control over the work, gives tasks and then receives reports about that task. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're now a head of the sector for analytics in the Ministry of the Interior; therefore, the officers of the analytics department are, in a way, accountable to you. They receive their tasks from you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, although you are the head of the sector for analytics, documentation and whatever the entire name of that sector is, you are superior only to the officers who are employed at the level of the republic, of the state, so who work in your analytics department. You are their superior officer?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm head for the employees in the sector for analytics, research and documentation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, similar departments or units exist also in the sector for internal affairs, sectors for internal affairs of the cities and municipalities. Individuals who work in those units are directly accountable to their heads for analytics and those heads are accountable to the municipal head of internal affairs and in the city of Skopje they're directly accountable to the assistant to the minister for the sector of internal affairs for the city of Skopje. Am I understanding the situation correctly?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, you are not the direct superior to those officers and they are not accountable to you directly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As we said a while ago the minister is also an authorised official as stipulated by law, but is it correct that the minister, regardless of whether this is the minister of the moment, the Minister Boskoski or Hari Kostov that was mentioned also, the minister has mainly political role within the ministry. Is that understanding of mine of the position of the minister correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister is usually a civilian and not necessarily a lawyer or a police officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you -- as you're employed in the Ministry of Interior have there other types of people, economists, sociologists and so on, other people employed in this ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The supervision line within the Ministry is such that this line goes through the line of the uniformed police and criminal police and on the other side, there's the line of state security. Are these the management lines within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The head of the bureau of public security, the director and the head of the bureau of the state security. There's also a director. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Both directors are appointed by the government with the caveat that of the ministry at the department of public security -- is being controlled by the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although the minister is a political person most of all, that the minister is an authorised official, manages the ministry mainly by bringing forth general acts for implementation of the law and performing the activities of the ministry such as rule books, directions based upon which the officers of the ministry act upon. Is this the manner through which the minister manages the ministry?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I say that also besides these types of management that the minister only directly performs certain activities that is given to him by the rule books of the organisation, mainly that -- with it is directly connected a department for finances, for international cooperation, personnel committee and so on. This -- are those bodies that are directly connected to the minister and not to the director of the public or state security. Is this -- are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the uniformed police and the units of the police, until August 2001 the minister had direct authority only over the -- a special unit Tiger and after that this unit also was included in the structure of the uniformed police and in the common line of the uniformed police. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the new organisational set-up of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were at one point working as a senior advisor in the legal sector, is it true that the legal department develops the legal acts that are passed by those people who are authorised to pass those acts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And a decision or -- the document that was used to appoint you at this position was prepared by the legal sector and the legal sector give you -- gave you this document, appointment document. I would like to ask that the witness be shown this decision. This is -- it is the T -- P375, MFI, 285.5.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 6379. Evidence -- exhibit 379, exhibit P379.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is -- in order to find it easier this is part of the document which is 65 ter 285.5. Ter. 65 ter 285.5. I apologise, maybe you will find it easier if I give you the number. ERN000-8906. ERN number 000-8906, and in the English one is ERN 000-8906-ET. In Macedonian, it's N000-8906.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Ms. Groseva, until we find the document, this document demonstrates that the decision that have been given to you, you received it from the legal -- from the department for legal issues and normative activities, it was signed by the head of the department, Suzana Nikodijevik-Filipovska. Do you remember that this document was shown to you? You have it now in front of you?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you've been given this decision and what we have -- and this was developed by the same, this decision was developed by the same department and the minister had signed this decision. Is that correct? This the way through which the minister signed it?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The decisions are drafted by the -- by the department for legal and personnel issues and they are signed by the minister of interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, as the case is with this decision, is this department based upon request of certain bodies, the personnel committee or the criminalistic police or other bodies within the ministry drafts -- develops the drafts of other acts and decision, that the minister signs after that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the legal department, the legal department develops the by-laws, decisions that the minister signs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The issue of the working relationship and the responsibilities of the officers are -- have also been set forth in a certain general act and in the ministry, besides the laws, we are talking about the collective agreement of the Ministry of the Interior, that have been co-signed with the union. However, --

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, besides these things that have been regulated with the collective agreement and the way that people are taken in the Ministry of Interior, can we say that there are certain other acts that can be used to regulate the conditions and the procedure through which people are employed, for example the conditions and the procedure through which employees are -- get their jobs in the special forces. In the ministry, the special cases in the ministry it is also possible to pass an act that determines the procedure, the conditions and the bodies that are hiring these officers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister on behalf of the ministry signs a decision for hiring of the employees after the procedure that has been followed or the procedure that has been developed by the rule book?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the minister never -- neither before the Minister Boskoski nor after him, the minister therefore does not sign the decision for the -- employment -- employment relations not on his on behalf only but on behalf of the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody claims in front of this Court that the minister was -- that the members, for example of the Lions, were signing their employment document with the minister that would be not true. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The collective agreement regulated the issues of the responsibility of the officers and the situations in which disciplinary procedure can be started or the responsibility -- the procedure through which the responsibility of the officer would be determined. That's the way with the collective agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This responsibility of the officers can be material or disciplinary. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The collective agreement also determines the bodies that can initiate such a procedure as well as the procedure that needs to be implemented in order to determine the responsibility of the officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole procedure that needs to be implemented, it is defined in the collective agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That procedure can be started only -- initiated against a non-person. In other words, we cannot have this kind of disciplinary procedure against a group of people or unknown perpetrators, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This procedure also must be implemented within a certain time-frame, otherwise this -- the terms of limitation might expire after which the disciplinary procedure might not be continued. Is that correct? ?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are familiar that the terms -- the statute of limitations of the disciplinary procedures are -- they expire and if there is a certain disciplinary infraction noted after the expiration of the statute of limitation, this procedure could not are started against this person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the disciplinary procedure is implemented by a permanent committee which is the disciplinary committee, and the mandate is usually determined by the mandate of the minister or with the selection of the minister or in some other manner but it has the composition that has been determined for many years. This is not a temporary committee; this is a standing committee.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, besides this temporary -- besides the standing committees which is the disciplinary within the ministry, there are other committees that have been created for very specific issues or ad hoc committees. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And depending on the purpose for which the committee had been established, the committee can be set up by the minister or another manager, and who issues the decision within which the composition, the task and other issues relating to this committee are set up?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The committees that have been established in such a manner, they cannot replace the authority of the bodies that have been indicated in the rule book for the organisation and the work of the Ministry of Interior nor can they be taken on by -- the task and responsibilities of other bodies; for example, the courts, the prosecutors and so on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The committee that you have discussed yesterday with my learned colleague, the committee that has been established by the minister Hari Kostov was one of these ad hoc committees. Therefore, established with a very specific task.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All members of the committee, as you, were authorised officials. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, just like you, those other members of the committee did not have the authority of the authorised officials from the -- from the operative part of the criminalistic police that are working in the pre-trial procedure according to the Law on Pre-trial Procedure in your country. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, to digress a little bit, according to the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Ministry of Interior, the police or the members of the Ministry of Interior cannot interrogate the citizens in the function of the witness that can be only done by the judge, according to the legal system. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police, within the pre-trial procedure, collects the information from the citizens based upon which it develops Official Notes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those information that the -- collected by the police from the citizens, that information can be either within the -- they can be in the form of an Official Note or minutes, because this procedure is not precisely defined in terms of what the -- the methods through which the police has to note down and write down the information it collects from the citizens. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you -- would you agree with me, Ms. Groseva, that based upon the form through which the information has been collected from the citizens, that information or statement that has been collected by the police from a citizen, regardless of whether it is based upon suspicion of this person provides some other information, this information or statement cannot be used in the criminal procedure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, this information -- it serves the police -- so it can corroborate other information, collect other evidence and prepare the criminal -- criminal report?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This criminal report if -- if the investigative judge has the responsibility to select this information, and in case the decision -- is based upon such -- based upon such information, this decision would be overturned. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that when I say that all -- all these interviews, statements, informations that you have collected within your committee and created within it, could not be treated as statements that police collects in the pre-trial procedure, especially because they do not have any legal standing in the criminal -- in the criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said yesterday, the sole task of the committee was to collect information for what was it that happened in the village of Ljuboten. We only collected information. We did not undertake investigation. This was no kind of procedure. Simply, the interviews with the colleagues were for the purpose of collecting information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my question was that these -- this was only information that were requested only by the minister and they were to be given to the minister.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information were only aimed to inform the minister in terms of what is it that the committee has done. Therefore, the purpose of the -- of the information that we have produced at the end was to inform the minister in terms of the activities undertaken by the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I fully agree that you explained this really well yesterday. But I had -- my question was an additional one and it is: Regardless of the fact that did you this job for the minister, this information that have you collected from the people, not material evidence but information that you have collected, had this information been made available to the court, this information would not be a good basis for court decisions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we see P379, MFI, Exhibit P379 which is 65 ter document 285.5, which is in Macedonian N000-8907; the English version is N000-8907-ET. Page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, you can see the decision on the screen. It was shown yesterday to you by my learned friend about the creation of the commission. It is dated the 7th of March --

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 2 of this decision, which is N000-8908 in Macedonian. And in English, it's N000-8907-N000-8908-ET, page 2. Page 2 in English, page 2 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see it on the screen. Your Honours, I have just been told that on page 18, line 14 my question was translated as follows. This information could not serve as a good basis for the Court. That's not what I said. What I said was that this information cannot be used --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Or, rather, would you please tell us, madam, whether these documents of yours could be used in court as evidence at all?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I couldn't recollect exactly my words so that's why I repeated the question to the witness. On page 2 which you have before you and since I'm using the Prosecution exhibits, I would like to ask my learned friends whether they have, by any chance, a hard copy of these documents so that it could be given to the witness. It might be of assistance to the witness. If they do not have the it, then I would ask the witness to look at the document on the screen. In item 2 of this decision, the tasks of your commission are set out quite specifically. And if I were to analyse this, I would say that the first task was to analyse all material, all documents in relation to the events in the area of the village of Ljuboten in August of 2001. Was that your first task?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then the following task --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Following that, you were given a task to establish the composition and the power or resources of the units which took over action in the period of time that followed, including the identity of each member of these units.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your third task was to establish the causes and circumstances of the death of the victims and the damage that ensued. Was that your third task? And then additional task was to -- to establish the truth surrounding these events and then you also had to inquire into the authority concerning the use of the units and the consequences of the operation which was carried out?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then this decision also specified the deadline, in item 3 it was specified that you were to complete your tasks by the 2nd of March 2003, item 3. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction the 2nd of May, 2003.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then following that, it is stated that it was your task to establish responsibility for the operation that was carried out in the area of the village of Ljuboten in August 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the previous paragraph it was also said that you should bear in mind the conclusions of the forensic medicine institute concerning the circumstances following the events of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This decision did not establish the method of operation of the commission. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This task, from item 2, paragraph 6, about establishing responsibility for the operation that was carried out, is the task that you, as commission, in accordance with the law and the rules of the ministry, --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asked by the interpreters to repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, as commission, have legal authority, in accordance with the law and the rules to establish responsibility, be it financial or disciplinary responsibility?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As we clarified before, the disciplinary responsibility is investigated by a special committee within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about criminal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the criminal responsibility, there is a specialised unit to investigate it. There are authorised officials employed there who are carrying out the investigations to ascertain the criminal responsibility and they work in cooperation with the courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this department can carry out only the actions specified in the law on pre-trial procedure and to supply the responsible prosecutor with its conclusions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is only pursuant to the request of the prosecutor that the criminal responsibility of a person can be established by a court. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is it correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you were given this task it was simply impossible to carry out this task legally speaking, from the legal point of view. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started working in the area where we believed we could complete our mission and that is, I will say again, to gather information about what has happened at Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Zoran Jovanovski, Major-General, was the president of this commission and at the time he was under-secretary in the Ministry of Interior. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned friend you said that you attended the meetings of this commission, that you took notes and that later on, based on those notes, you drafted proposal -- proposal of information from the members of the commission, and following any remarks received, you forwarded this information to the minister. Did I understand your task within the commission correctly?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given that this decision did not regulate the method of work of this commission, would you please tell us who was the one to determine the method of work of the commission?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those ad hoc committees, to use your term, there is always a representative of the sector for analytics, research and documenting participating as a member. And it is an unwritten rule. So this is the practice in our work. The representative of the analytics department is in charge of -- just of drafting the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in accordance with this established practice, you interpreted your duties within the commission and acted in accordance with that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even though you were appointed as a full member of the commission?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And yesterday you said that you did not attend the first meeting of the commission, if I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I had a business trip to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the commission operate at that time without a representative of the sector for analytics?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was another representative of the analytics sector in attendance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that person was there as member of the commission, even though that person was not appointed to the commission by the minister. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, on page 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Ms. Residovic, is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the break then and resume in 20 minutes' time, at 20 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, Ms. Groseva, I mentioned that yesterday, and it is on page 4712, you have mentioned that in the committee the standard procedure -- the committee was working under standard procedure. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, Ms. Groseva, just to check whether I have understood you well. What is the standard procedure that the committee uses; namely, is it correct that -- that you have invited certain individuals at the meetings of the committee using two avenues. The members of the employees of the Ministry of Interior, you would call them on the phone and those individuals that were not members of the ministry, that is civilians, you were subpoenaed -- you sent subpoenas?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, summons.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those individuals that were invited with summons, i.e., civilians, you have warned them when you were invited them that they had the right to call an attorney with them, as well as what the consequences would -- what the consequences would have been in case they did not respond to this summons. That is, you have pointed them out that according to Article 142.3, that they will be brought in by force. Was this the manner through which you called the civilians to attend?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed -- has shown you the invitation that was given to Johan Tarculovski, and that is the manner through which you have invited this individual. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters wish to indicate that there is a noise of typing coming and it bothers us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this, in this procedure, as I -- if I understood well, I would like to corroborate this, would the members of the committee, other members of the committee led the interview, you were -- and you were the person who took the minutes of the work. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This standard procedure was such that after the interview the person that was otherwise an officer of the Ministry of Interior, that person created his or her own Official Note, and in case this person was not a member of the Ministry of Interior, then there were minutes -- minutes were developed after the interview with this person. Was this the next step in the standard procedure of your commission?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based upon the -- I just want to note that the witness about this on page 4717 and page 4736 of the transcript. And according -- you mentioned that within this procedure that based upon your own notes, you were responsible to develop -- to write the draft of the information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you have mentioned yourself, you were submitting this information to the members of the committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: If on the meetings of this committee -- if not all members of the committee had been present, whether this information that you wrote was submitted only to those who had been present at that interview or also to those members who were not present at the moment?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to those who were present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown the information of May 6th about the meeting at which you were not present -- at which you had not been present. This information was not given to you. You could have only seen that information after it was entered and registered in your department of analytics. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also said that on May 28th, at the meeting of the committee, the president, General Jovanovski, was not present. Please tell me: The information that was shown to you yesterday, whether it had been submitted to the General Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In order to inform him as the president of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you have stated that your own notes -- you did not keep your own notes because they were not an official document and they had been consequently destroyed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Official Notes that were handwritten by those individuals that were interviewed, as well as the minutes of those individuals, you did not destroy. They were part of the information and the materials of the committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Upon the approval of the information by the committee, this information would have become a document. It was subsequently submitted to the minister and was registered in your department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the way I have explained my understanding, that the standard procedure which you attempted to explain yesterday, this is the manner through which you use -- to which you worked from the moment the committee was set up until November 25. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You -- because you have already mentioned that the committee had the task to collect the information for the minister, the minister was the person that had individual responsibility to decide what to do with this information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the decision made by the committee, we were able to see that the committee -- it was -- consisted of -- was diverse, it had both in terms of ethnic background and in terms of professional background. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood well, there were two Albanians, one Bosnian and the rest of the committee members were Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I have never looked at the committee that way. They are all my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Hamdi, last name unclear, Baftijari was Albanian. Five, Besim Ramicevic is Bosnian -- is Bosniak, Muslim?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article -- number 6, the person under number 6, Sefset Surlaj was also Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Albanian. Interpreter's correction, Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had the decision of the committee in front of you. I would like you to follow this so we can follow along. ERN N000-8907, and the English is just ET, page 1. It is Exhibit P379, MFI. Based upon the professional responsibilities within the Ministry of Interior, this committee was also very diverse. We can look all the members from the ministry who were part of it. The Major-General, the under-secretary in the police department was the chairman. The second member was from the -- from the forensic sector of the crime police department.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The third person was also from the crime police department?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fourth member, as well as the president, was from the police department?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fifth was the chief of the section for violent crimes, sex crimes, traffic crimes, juvenile delinquency and socio-pathological phenomenon, the sector for general crimes. And the sixth person was the senior inspector in the unit for professional standards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, you were representing the department for analytics?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given this composition of the committee, would you agree with me when I say that the minister could have relied that -- could have believed that the committee would do its job properly, and that the minister could rely on the information that you gave to him?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of this committee were colleagues who had many years of experience, each of them in their own respective profession which, of course, guaranteed a quality performance of the job.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show the Exhibit P73 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were well-known that Minister Boskoski on August 13th, 2001, right after the events that took place in Ljuboten set up the committee. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from what I've read from the media to this day. But not at the moment then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that during the work of your committee in 2003, you did not have the decision for setting up the committee set up by Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not have at your disposal the report on the information produced by this committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, yes what? Did you have that information or not?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- we did not have the report from this committee. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In front of you now, you have the decision for establishing a committee. And I will not ask you about the decision itself or the tasks because you were not aware of this decision. However, do you know Goran Mitevski, or do you know what his position was in 2001?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, director of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you also know that he was a police officer for many years, that he was a distinguished professional, and that he is a trustworthy person. Is that how you accepted your director at that moment or do you have another opinion of him?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the cooperation from the director, he is a distinguished professional. He is an expert in his work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Risto Galevski and do you know what kind of job -- what kind of job did he have in -- at that time?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Risto Galevski was the head of the department for police, and we had an ongoing cooperation with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me when I say that in 2001 had -- about 20 years of experience in the police, that he was very distinguished, that he had an enormous professional experience and that he was honest person?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This opinion of Goran Mitevski and Risto Galevski, you had no reason to change your opinion of them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The way you gave the answer sounds like you gave the -- different answers, therefore I'm going to repeat my question. And my question is: Whether you have ever changed your opinion of Goran Mitevski and Risto Galevski changed over the past few years. Please -- and give me an answer with a whole sentence.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My opinion for Mr. Mitevski and Mr. Galevski, they are exceptional professionals, and experts in their area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know Zivko Petrovski?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was head of the department for analytics briefly where I was working.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that in 2001, he was the head of the department of criminal police?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the same way that Minister Kostov could rely on you as professional individuals who do their job properly, professionally and in the best manner possible, would you agree with me if I said that by selecting the most responsible individuals in the Ministry of Interior, distinguished professionals, that Minister Boskoski wanted to collect the best possible information at that moment, the best possible information available at that moment?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in my opinion, he would not have been able to find better professionals at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And considering that they were heads of -- of the entire structure of the Ministry of Interior, they had available, they had an opportunity to gather information and to communicate with all structures of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When one has in mind the offices they held and the duties they performed at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The information that such person would draft, the information note would be a reliable basis for a minister, Minister Boskoski or any other minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Considering that they are professionals with long years of service, experts in their area and professionals.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we reviewed the tasks for your committee, and I would like to ask to see again the page 2 of this document. That is N000-8908, Macedonian, and the English is the same number with the ET appended. That is the Exhibit P379, MFI. One of the tasks was for you to gather all the materials, all the documents. Could you agree with me, Ms. Groseva, that you did not have then available the documents that the forensics department of the police compiled in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which documents are you referring?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, analysis of the weapons found at the scene, then the paraffin glove test, and any other documents existing at the forensics department of the police. Did you obtain those documents?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain, did you have available the documents that the operations department of the forensics police department of the Cair department within the sector for internal affairs, Skopje, compiled in August 2001, aiming to gather data about the casualties, about the deaths, about the perpetrators? Did you have these documents available?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the committee started working, we had no documents. Apart from -- this is now my recollection, long time has passed. Documents from the forensics medicine institute were available or it was so mentioned but those documents were not reviewed by the committee. It was known that there were such materials available from the forensics medicine institute, but these materials were not reviewed, and the committee did not have any other type of materials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you did not have access to the documents that the Ministry of Interior gathered upon the request of the court and communicated to the court, and you did not have available any of the documents that the court had available?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were not given any materials of the international organisations that were in Skopje at that time, in 2001, or had compiled any information related to the Ljuboten events. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No such materials were made available to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The office of the ICTY Prosecutor that was, at that time, located in Skopje, also never submitted to you any information or the -- or documents that it had available at that time?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we never received any information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood, you had the task to communicate the information that you produced or the information that you would receive to the minister. You, as a committee, had no powers or authority to communicate the information to third parties outside of the Ministry of Interior, be it local or international organisations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I repeat: The information were intended just to inform the minister about the work of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the information produced on 6th of May, and that is Exhibit P379, MFI, 65 ter 285.24. That is N000-8956, that is the first page of the information note, while the English version is at N000-8957-ET, first page. This is the first information note from the meeting that you did not attend. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I understood the procedure, in accordance with it, you had invited, as we can see from the document, Gjorgji Mitrov, Zivko Gacovski, Johan Tarculovski, and Goce Ralevski to come meet with you on that date. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Borce Vasilevski was invited as well, but he did not respond to the invitation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend the meeting but this is what is written in the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Gjorgji Mitrov, Zivko Gacovski, Johan Tarculovski, at the time were employed by the MUP and they that were invited to attend on the phone?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what you said, Goce Ralevski who was a civilian and worked in Sobranje [phoen] was supposed to have received a summons?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, there is no evidence of any summons within the documents of the police. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even though three workers of the MUP were interviewed, it was shown to you that the Official Note was written only by Johan Tarculovski, in his own hand. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So even though Mitrov and Gacovski were both members of the MUP or Ministry of Interior, this first meeting did not follow the procedure you described and these persons never produced their own handwritten notes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Goce Ralevski as a civilian was not only not invited to attend in the way that you described, but also no record was produced about what he had said. So in relation to him, the routine procedure as you described it was not followed either at this meeting held on the 6th of May. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information you produced inevitably had to contain all of the facts that you had heard or that the persons wrote in their own Official Notes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I had produced provided a summary, an overview of what has been said by the colleagues. Therefore, in some cases, you can see different wording, different terms used in the information note from what is written in the Official Note that the colleague had submitted. However, I will say again that the information note had a single purpose, to inform the minister on what the committee was doing. And on the basis of that information, nobody undertook any activities and no procedure was carried out further. That was the information with a purpose to just inform the minister about the activity of the committee, so it is not necessary that part of the conversation with a colleague is interpreted verbatim and so fully corresponds with the note compiled by that colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not send to the minister these handwritten notes, rather, you only sent information to him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this information or report produced by your colleagues on page 2, Johan Tarculovski allegedly said before the members of the commission, and you yourself were not in attendance there, that Ljube Boskoski personally called him in and ordered him to shed light on the case because it was suspected that Xhavid Asani had been in Ljuboten. Do you remember that this was stated in this report or information?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown handwritten notes written on that same day or on the following day by your colleague, Johan Tarculovski, who, at the time, was an inspector?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now be shown P379 MFI N000-8922. The English version is N000-8922-ET-01.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see here that up in the corner it says in the English text the 3rd of March, 2003, whereas this interview took place at the meeting of the commission held on the 5th of May. So obviously this is a mistake in translation, because you did not even exist as a commission on the 3rd of March, 2003, correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Further, you can see here in this Official Note written personally by Johan Tarculovski and signed by him in his own hand, that he wrote as follows: There was intelligence from the villagers that Xhavid Asani was in the village and several houses and so on. So in the text written by your colleague, the then inspector Tarculovski, Ljube Boskoski is not mentioned at all. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that when your colleague wrote this information for the minister he in fact gave him in the very least, incomplete information, because had it been true that Tarculovski said this about Boskoski at the meeting, there should also be there text to the effect that not only he did not say this, but something quite contrary was included in the handwritten text?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that there are discrepancies between what is presented in the information note and what is presented in the Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the minister didn't know that, because he did not receive the Official Note. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, I'm looking for the precise word. This is not of decisive importance because the minister is only informed about any, and I repeat, any measures that should possibly be taken. The normal course would be to complete the entire set of documents and to submit the complete set of documents to the minister or to anyone else, to present the complete documents available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, would you agree with me that had the minister received information only from the one side and not from the other, that Tarculovski mentioned Boskoski and that on the second occasion it was said that he received information from the villagers, then that would imply that the minister was not informed about the information available to the commission?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that this is not the case with Mr. Johan only. There are other statements; if you read them, there are discrepancies there as well. So the purpose was to inform the minister what persons have been interviewed, what was the course of the interview, what information had been received, but I can agree with you that still this is not data of minor importance. This is essential data that the committee should have clarified so that it is known --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your first report, Minister Boskoski was mentioned without any reason, even though Tarculovski in his handwritten document did not state this at all.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should have been clarified. This was a discrepancy, contradictory notion between the Official Note and the data mentioned in the information note so that we arrive at the understanding where the omission was made.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the speakers to wait for the interpretation to be finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It seems that there's a mistake in your answer, when you wanted to clarify something. It is stated here that there is a discrepancy in the date. Would you please slowly repeat your answer, because there was no mention of the date in your answer, rather, you mentioned an important fact that needs to be included in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So would you please tell us: Is it true that the information supplied to the minister did not contain an important fact which differed from what was stated in the report and which was included in the handwritten document of Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that there are -- that there is a discrepancy regarding part of the statement of Mr. Tarculovski, from what you read in the information that has been officially submitted to the minister and his Official Note which has been - as far as I know - produced immediately after his interview. Considering the fact that the data, the fact is important, the committee should have undertook activities to clarify this fact, to see what is at the root of this discrepancy, is it the officer who produced the note, or was it Mr. Tarculovski when writing his Official Note, because his statement was given before all -- many members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were not in attendance so you cannot confirm what he has stated or not?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed to you yesterday the document that was disclosed to the Defence, which is information or report dated the 28th of May, 2003. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The president of the commission did not attend this meeting, and you did not interview anyone on that occasion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you were told that there were some documents that had been furnished to the commission. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on page 1, it is stated, first of all, that in the reply to the cable sent to the security sector, Skopje, a report was sent that in the stated period of time in the village of Ljuboten, members of active and reserve forces from the SVR Skopje, police stations Cair and Mirkovci, were deployed at the check-points Chinese wall, Straiste and Busalak and that these check-points had been operational previously as well. Further, it was stated that on the 12th of August, 2001 at around 1600 hours, in order to block a road, the village of Ljuboten -- or rather, in order to block the road between the village of Ljuboten and Cair from the -- or, rather, two platoons were established by the Skopje SVR; one of the platoons belonged to the SVR of Skopje, and the other platoon belonged to the rapid intervention unit called the Lions, and that their task was to ensure safe passage of the citizens leaving the village of Ljuboten on their way to Skopje. Do you remember that this was written in your information or report?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was produced on the basis of answers received from several services or units within the Ministry of Interior, and upon the request of the committee to send a cable to them so that they reply on the 12th of August, where were the police members deployed, police members belonging to each of those organisational units. What you are reading now is the reply from the sector for internal affairs, SVR Skopje, as far as I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the same report or information you stated that had you received a piece of information or some kind of a report from the commander of the unit for terrorist activities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That the unit Lions was not established then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the unit for anti-terrorist activities is actually something that used to be known as rapid intervention unit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the speakers not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it was known as the rapid intervention battalion, known as Lions, or lavovi. And you have already told us that the commander of that unit informed you that the Lions had not been in Ljuboten because on the 12th of August, they did not exist at all. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We had a witness testify before this Court, Risto Galevski. In your own words, he is an outstanding professional, and at that time he was the head of the unit of uniformed policemen, the entire department of uniformed police. Would you agree with me that he is a person who knew which units were part of the Ministry of Interior and that he also knew whether the Lions existed or not?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering his long years of service, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if General Risto Galevski, before this Court testified that the Lions had not been in Ljuboten for the simple reason that in August of 2001 they did not exist, then we could rely on his words. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Apologies. But it's to this particular question I would object as I don't believe this witness could speak to this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already answered this question, Your Honours. Had she been unable to answer, she would not have answered. However, I can see now that the answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it should not be.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware who is Goran Georgievski?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if you do not know him, I will not show to you what Goran Georgievski stated to the OTP investigators. You had contradictory information from the commander of, as you say SVR Skopje as well, and did you not attempt to clarify which of the information is correct. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this information of 28th of May, you indicated that you were informed that there is some information about the events at Ljuboten village according to which - allegedly - some persons arrived to the Cair police station to demand to be issued weapons. Do you recall having written this in your information?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it also correct that this information was never submitted to the committee and you never saw this information personally?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That kind of information was submitted to the commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, it is not included in the documents of the commission. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These things that were submitted here to the Court, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who produced that information?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. When answering my learned friend's questions, you said that you also produced the report or information on the 25th of November, 2003. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown Exhibit P379, MFI, 65 ter document 285.6, N000-8909; that's the Macedonian version. And then the English version is N000-8944.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this report or information being shown to you?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that that document included information about the interviews held between the 12th and 20th of November, 2003. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to that, or, rather, on the first day of your work, on the 12th of November, you interviewed Johan Tarculovski again.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this occasion, just like in his Official Note, Johan Tarculovski did not mention in any way Minister Boskoski in relation to the events in Ljuboten. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have before you the report or information 871 drafted on the 25th of November, 2003. If we look at this information, on page N000-8991, the Macedonian version, and N000-8946, then we could see that the commission --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is now page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- namely, that the commission talked with the employees of the ministry Vladimir Cagorovic, Ljube Krstevski and Vanco Ginovski. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to that you said that on the 12th you also interviewed Zoran Jovanovski, known as Bucuk. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
