utterances.text: Following that in your information, it is stated that you interviewed Ljupco Bliznakovski also on the 20th of November, which can be seen on page 6 of this information. It seems that the ERN numbers and pages are not correct. Therefore, you said there that you interviewed Ljupco Bliznakovski, Pero Stojanovski and Trajce Kuzmanovski. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the last page, you stated that you also interviewed Radojko Lozanovski and Miodrag Stojanovski. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since there is no English text, we cannot see the page that I mentioned, because these are voluminous documents. It says on my copy that is N000-8949, and page 6 of this document; and then the one we see in Macedonian is page 3 on the document. This one we can see in Macedonian on the screen right now is page 3 of the information in the English version. Your Honours, perhaps is not essential for us to see it on the screen. I'm reading from the document which is Exhibit P379, and if the witness is in the position to answer, then she should do so, because it is obvious that we are experiencing some problems with calling them on the screen. And since they don't have the appropriate numbers in e-court, they are difficult to locate. And perhaps it would be a good time for the break, if we are going to respect what you said at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... We will have a break now and resume at five past 5.00, and hopefully matters will be in order by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, you still have in front of you the information on 25th of November, 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask now that the screen displays page 3 in the Macedonian version N000-8991, while the English is N000-8946. And as you stated a while ago, it can be seen here that on the 19th of November, 2003, you questioned Vladimir Cagorovic, Ljube Krstevski and Vanco Ginovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that on the previous page it was just noted that on the 12th, Johan Tarculovski and Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, were questioned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the page 12 in the Macedonian. That is N000-8915, while the English is N000-8949. And here, in the second paragraph, in Macedonian, and the first paragraph in the English version, read that on the 28th of November, 2003, you questioned Ljupco Bliznakovski and Pero Stojanovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph at the English page and that is at the following page in Macedonian, N000-8916, reads that you also interviewed Trajce Kuzmanovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the last page of the information, and that is Macedonian N000-8917 and English N000-8950, read that you interviewed Radojko Lozanovski and Miodrag Stojanovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So between the 12th and the 25th, you interviewed Miodrag Stojanovski, Radojko Lozanovski, Ljube Krstevski, Vanco Ginovski Vladimir Cagorovic, Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, Ljupco Bliznakovski, Pero Stojanovski, and Trajce Kuzmanovski. Are these all the persons that you interviewed during that period?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among those individuals - Ljupco Bliznakovski, Pero Stojanovski and Radojko Lozanovski - although they are officers of the Ministry of Interior, did not produce Official Notes which was in accordance with your standard procedure. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not confirm this. Maybe their Official Notes are contained in the dossier of the committee, in the files of the committee, however, they were not requested or maybe they were not submitted. But it is also possible that they had not produced such notes. I really could not answer this question, neither in affirmative nor in negative.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, and Trajce Kuzmanovski were not members of the MOI?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they needed written summons. However, there is no evidence that they were invited through such written summons and there are no minutes compiled on their interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When I asked you previously, you answered that you did not have the authority to communicate the information to other parties outside of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I clarify this briefly? So in the Ministry of Interior, there is a procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information submitted to the minister of the interior, if there is a need to submit to external users or parties outside of the Ministry of Interior, such information are then redrafted, meaning that we use initials instead of persons' names. Not all issues are presented in such informations, so there is a procedure in which way the leadership of the Ministry of Interior is informed and also there is a procedure for communicating such information outside of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement in paragraph 7, you stated that you communicated the information also to Besim Ramicevic, who was the liaison officer for the Prosecutor of the ICTY. Do you remember having said this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering what you stated previously, tell me, were you authorised for this by the minister or did you do this because you believed he should be communicated such information?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information were communicated to Besim Ramicevic who was the liaison officer upon his request. So an official request was submitted to the analytics department that for the needs of the ICTY, he needs certain information to be submitted to him. However, the feedback on how he forwarded those information, whether he had forwarded just the originals or whether he had redrafted those, I did not receive such feedback. So that is a communication between two employees of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, the analytics department, could be requested information by other heads in the ministry and you had the duty to submit information to them as well.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So communicating information to Ramicevic, the liaison officer, you considered to be not your duty in your capacity of the committee member, but, rather, in your capacity of the head of the analytics sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no discussion in the committee meetings about communicating information produced by the committee. That was rather, a communication between two services, two units within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And considering that you believed that this was internal communication, you did not inform the committee about that fact, that you communicated all the information to Besim Ramicevic who was the liaison officer with the ICTY. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that we look now at the Exhibit P251, MFI, which bears the Macedonian number N000-6433, while the English page is numbered N000-6433-N000-6435-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information notes that the Ministry of Interior communicated and it was signed -- the last page of it was signed by Besim Ramicevic was shown to you yesterday by my learned friend, the Prosecutor. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That information is written on the 16th of June, 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was submitted to the office of the ICTY in Skopje, handed personally to Mr. Andrzej Cidlik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how was it submitted. I did not produce this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether it is written here --

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The subject of this information is: Report on activities to date concerning the investigation into events in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among other things, if we look now at the page 2 of this document, and that is Macedonian N000-6434, and English N000-6433-N000-6435-ET, you see here then on the second page, in the Macedonian version in the last paragraph, while in the English version that is the third paragraph from the bottom, that it reads here that Johan Tarculovski had stated that he had been an inspector in the sector for security and that the minister Ljube Boskoski, personally called him and gave him orders to resolve the situation related to the presence of suspect Xhavid Asani at Ljuboten village. Do you see this written here?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, this part, this information that was sent to the ICTY office is based only on the first information of the 6th of May, the meeting that did you not attend, so you don't know what Johan Tarculovski actually stated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This information does not state that Johan Tarculovski wrote in his own hand the information where he did not mention Ljube Boskoski at all, where he actually mentioned completely different sources of information about Xhavid Asani. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in this way, a completely unverified and completely incomplete information was sent outside of the ministry, not what the committee had available at that time?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this statement, if we look at it again, if we look at the information, now at the page 3, and that is N000-6435, and the English version is N000-6433-N000-6435-ET. It mentions here in the last paragraph in the English version, and in the second paragraph of this Macedonian version information, it mentions the individual Ljube Krstevski, head of the OVR Cair, who had ordered that the issuance of weapons is not allowed; but that on the following date, on the 11th of August, 2001, he informed the administrator of this station via mobile phone that upon the order of a superior officer from the MOI, he should issue weapons and equipment to persons who are present there. Do you remember that when we were looking at your information of 25th of November we ascertained - actually, you confirmed - that you had interviewed Ljube Krstevski and Radojko Lozanovski who is that administrator, only in the period between the 12th and the 25th of November. So do you agree that it was only then that you received certain information from these individuals?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you remember --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could look again that information, and I will try to find the part which states what Ljube Krstevski stated. That is the page -- Macedonian page is N000-8912, and the English is N000-8946. It is a part of Exhibit P379, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you managed to find this page of the information, you see there that Ljube Krstevski allegedly said to your committee that he received such order from Ljupco Bliznakovski and it reads precisely: "On the 11th of August, around 2200 hours by the deputy Stojanovski Pero and Bliznakovski Ljupco, I received an order together with the army representative Major Despodov to go to the village of Ljuboten and establish contact with Johan and the others." Do you agree with me, again, that the information that was sent to the office of the International Tribunal in Skopje about what Ljube Krstevski allegedly stated, persons -- person who had not been interviewed by the committee by that time is again a crude mistake in presenting the information obtained by the committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this note, this note is signed by Mr. Ramicevic on behalf of the Ministry of Interior. But the fact is that the committee materials were used, and with regards to this part where he mentions the head Ljube Krstevski, I am really unable to say whether data came from, whether he had received the data through operative channels, because at that time he could not have had information from the committee about an interview with the head Ljube Krstevski because there has not been such interview at that time, and I really could not answer where the information came from, where he had received this information from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, from what you answered previously, Besim Ramicevic, was not authorised by the committee to communicate the information anywhere outside the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The committee never discussed communicating information outside of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Besim Ramicevic as a member of the committee never informed you that he communicated all the information from the committee to the office of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information that information are communicated, but when I was visited by the ICTY for the first time, it was then that I saw that the original documents were submitted, the original information note. I thought that the information was redrafted, processed, not submitted the original, the entire information, the information note in the entirety. I only saw it when I was visited -- when I was interviewed for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you saw then that absolutely unverified information were sent, that you could not ascertain later within the committee, also about Ljube Boskoski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you stated - this is also written in the committee decision - that Besim Ramicevic is head of the department for violent crime. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Besim Ramicevic ever inform you as a committee member about the activities that he himself and his department undertook within the ministry in 2001?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which activities? I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Activities at Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Besim Ramicevic ever inform you as a committee member that the ministry made a proposal after the on-site investigation failed and after it was impossible to ascertain what has happened at the village, did he inform that you the initiative -- that the ministry made a motion to the prosecutor's office and to the court in Skopje to perform exhumation of the bodies in the village?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe that was discussed, but any such document that such initiative has been made, the committee hasn't seen. But maybe in the discussions between them, between the committee members that was mentioned, but in the preparatory work, in the agreeing what the committee will do. But the documents, official materials, we have not seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Besim Ramicevic ever inform you that he, on behalf of the ministry, attended the meetings with the prosecutor, the judge, forensic medicine experts, discussing with them how to conduct exhumation and post-mortem and that he produced a written document on this topic?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give you the same answer. Maybe he had verbally mentioned something you and gave certain proposals, but we have not -- but he had failed to submit anything in a written form to the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood you well. You had no documents whatsoever concerning the measures that had been taken in order to clarify and look into the situation in the events in the village of Ljuboten in 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given the discrepancies that exist in the information that was put to you, discrepancies between what one person said - we looked into what Johan Tarculovski said - and we saw that there were three different versions of that. Given that that was the state of affairs, did you attempt at any point in time to verify further these facts?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a committee?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our practice, this is something that would have been done at the very end of the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We could also see there that there was a statement by, say, Gjorgji Mitrov and by Zivko Gacovski, who describe completely differently the issuance of weapons. That was another fact that in your view did not need to be further verified and so on. You simply wrote down who said what. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Ljube Krstevski's statement you also wrote down that he received orders from Bliznakovski and Stojanovski; whereas what they themselves stated was completely contrary to what Ljube Krstevski said. This is yet another piece of information that you never verified. You simply wrote down who said what. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because as I had clarified earlier our task was just to collect information. We were not conducting an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in your information, in your reports, there were several versions and essentially you never reached any conclusion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was clear to you, wasn't it, that the persons you interviewed did not have an obligation to speak the truth before your commission. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not conduct an investigation. We just had an interview with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is why you never cautioned any of these persons about their rights, that they could have, be it as witnesses or suspects, because, simply, you were not authorised to caution them on their rights. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is for those reasons that your commission never attempted to carry out the last task in that decision, to establish the responsibility. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So even though you worked for eight months rather than for two months as you were initially instructed in the decision, you never established responsibility of anyone who could have killed somebody in the village.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have the authority to nominate somebody as a suspect or to investigate. Our goal was to gather information in order to find out what is it that happened in Ljuboten. So we had no intention to make somebody a formal suspect. As a committee, we had no authority like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never even received information about somebody killing somebody. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not receive any piece of information about somebody setting a house on fire.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based upon the statements that we got from our colleagues, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to mistreatment of persons, you only had information provided by Krstevski that 15 members of the army mistreated some persons. You had no other information about this. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if this information were true, then police could not institute any proceedings against members of the army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the persons interviewed provided information that on the Radishan road, which was blocked, the police went there to assist and to separate civilians from the villagers of Ljuboten and to prevent further unfavourable developments. I simply summarized what some of the interviewed persons said. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So even had you been an authorised official who was authorised to make an inquiry into this, you still would not have been able to institute any disciplinary action against civilians or members who were not employed by the Ministry of Interior. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the work you conducted, you did not gather a single fact which could imply that a specific person from the ministry went beyond their authorities.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based upon what we received as information, as data, such information were not presented to us in any of the interviews with our colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have just one more question concerning this and then I will turn briefly to some other topics concerning your professional duties. If I were to tell you that at the time there were certain people and certain forces who wanted to -- to frame Minister Boskoski at any cost, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know what to tell you, what to answer you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's a very honest answer. Thank you. However, after there was a change in the government, great purges were carried out in the Ministry, and many persons close to Boskoski were removed from office. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now have I just a few more questions concerning your work. Is it true that you within the analytics department tried to preserve the document in accordance with the regulations that regulate this to the extent possible?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector for analytics, according to the rules, we archive and document -- of documentation from the area of public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, would you agree with me that in 2001, during the crisis, it was very difficult to fulfil this task.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The situation in 2001 was extraordinary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it could be said that all of you worked around the clock?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in order to preserve your documentation, if what I was told was true, you had to do the following. From the area of Tetovo which was particularly at risk, you had to remove some documentation in order to preserve it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. They were brought in the archive of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, due to numerous events, frequently, the information was not communicated in the normal procedure, but, rather was conveyed by phone. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the forwarding of information in the ministry is done according to Rule book that concerns this. But, however, you said yourself in 2001 you were working under in a situation with an armed conflict was present. The way we disseminated information then was in such a way that we all deviated from these rules. Therefore, we would inform people over the phone. Sometimes we would do it orally. The written information was sometimes late, but the circumstances under which we worked were such at that time. However, for every event we disseminated the information and the relevant materials were forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It could happen that some verbal information was not recorded so there was really nothing for you to preserve. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was possible. Especially in the crisis days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, if an investigative judge noted down that the operations centre on duty informed him back on the 12th in the afternoon that there were dead bodies in Ljuboten, then the ministry carried out its task regardless of whether the information on this was recorded and preserved in the ministry or not.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task was completed, but I'm pretty sure there was written information about it. I say this with the confidence of 15 years working in the department of analytics. And I'm sure that those -- that that information is available in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, even if somebody dutifully noted down that piece of information, it could have also happened that during that period of time you used a special paper for cables that used to fade away very fast and, basically, was illegible after a year. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: True, that was a very serious problem but those were the circumstances under which we had to operate. After a year, the only thing we were left was a white sheet of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, naturally, you destroyed such sheets of paper because they were useless.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Naturally, your work depended on the skills and qualifications of people who worked in police stations and departments of internal affairs. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It could have also happened that they failed to convey a certain piece of information. In that case, it would have been impossible for you to establish whether something had happened or not.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will reiterate. Those were extraordinary circumstances. It was difficult to inform people, considering the situation because part of the people, employees from the analytics department had to go in the field when a case -- when the situation required that. However, we kept disseminating information and I'm sure the failure to find a document does not mean that that document does not exist. That document can be in a completely different file because, unfortunately, the Ministry of Interior does not archive the documents electronically; we do not scan our documents or put them on microfiche. This is something that we do manually. And it is expected that in such a huge number of materials for something to be misplaced, to be put in a different file place other than the one that is proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now that have you mentioned this. It is true that it's only in the last year or two during your term as head that the documentation is archived in a proper way, and this is why it is very difficult to establish whether a document is misplaced or lost completely, because this was not done in a proper way previously.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. This is a very serious problem and I will tell you this, you can understand it any way you want. I had been -- I was an analyst myself and I have misplaced documents. There are piles and piles of materials and it just happens that every now and then that the -- I couldn't file the file in the -- the document in the proper file and then it turns up somewhere else. Now we are going through this archive and reorganising it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I have just a few more questions relating to your work. All the basic information stemming from people in the field, from policemen on duty in police stations and so on, are forwarded to the department of the internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this same information is sent to the department for analytics, within that same department of internal affairs. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This department includes all the most important events in its report or information which is then further sent to Skopje, to the sector for analytics. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Skopje sector has several departments, and it produces a document called information on a daily basis or on a basis of different topics where they condense the most important events based on the information that they had received and they sent this condensed information to you, to the sector for analytics. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just as you in MVR receive information from the territory of the entire state, you then draft a report on weekly events or daily events, depending on what the situation is and then this information produced to you is sent to senior officials within the security field or to ministers and so on, or perhaps to the under-secretary for police, depending who is competent for the information that you compiled. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, these cables, Official Notes and so on, is it delivered to the minister on a daily basis, all of that?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all telegrams and information from the regional offices are submitted to the ministry; and to the minister, I can say that they're almost never forwarded because the minister receives processed information that are made available to him with them. His day starts with a daily bulletin about the security issues and activities on the territory of Republic of Macedonia and the sector for analytics and research submits this information. They're not telegrams, they're not Official Notes from the regional organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that's how it was before Mr. Boskoski. This is it how the minister used to be informed when Mr. Boskoski was in the office and this is how the ministers are informed nowadays. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now each minister, the ministers before Boskoski, then Mr. Boskoski and then ministers after Mr. Boskoski, relied on the information received from the entire ministry via different specialist channels. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Because I have to do my job responsibly and professionally. Mistakes happen but in the communication with the minister, we point out our mistakes, we correct them, but 90 per cent of the cases everything is done professionally and in an expert manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, finally, if the minister needed to request some information from the ministry, say, somebody from outside the ministry requested the minister to inform him about something or to deliver some documents, would it be proper for the minister to send this request to his under-secretary for police, his under-secretary for crime police, and his official or head of the sector for analytics asking them to reply to this request so that he, in turn, could forward this information to the party requesting it?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to correct you by saying that it was submitted to the director of public security and the director of public security was forwarded to the sector of analytics because the whole communication and correspondence with other ministries, with the government are realised through the sector for analytics and research or -- or also with international organisation. We do this communication through the sector for analytics and research.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the minister could never sit himself and write an information or go to the field to investigate something?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much,, Ms. Groseva.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. I think it might be a convenient time to take the next break now and we would resume at 25 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm reminded that it could be useful, Mr. Apostolski, to inquire how long you anticipate being.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hope to finish the cross-examination of this witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that include re-examination? Give it some serious thought during the break, Mr. Apostolski. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, witness Tatjana Groseva, my name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with Jasmina Zivkovic we defend Mr. Johan Tarculovski. You were the member of the committee that investigated the circumstances and the factual situation about the activities of the village of Ljuboten on the period of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Besides you, there were six other members of the committee, so that brings a total of seven members of the committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what was the minimum number of people necessary in order for the committee to start working?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not such a number. In case somebody was absent, the reasons for that person's absence were identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were not present at the first meeting. Is it correct that -- that Mr. Emilio Frisic did not attend any of the committee's meetings?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, in case if somebody was not present and I thought you were able to see that in the information where it had been stated that -- an issue of information the people absent are listed together with the reasons for their absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the interview with Johan Tarculovski, he was not informed of his right to -- to remain silent and not answer any of these questions?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the meeting of the committee at which I was present?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For both.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At which I was not present, I cannot tell you about those at which I was not present, but I think is an important fact and that would have been listed in the information. However, I was not present at this meeting. At the second interrogation of Mr. Tarculovski, besides -- apart from telling him that he has the right to have his own attorney, no other -- he was not informed of any of his other rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Johan Tarculovski had not been cautioned and warned that these statements -- that the statements that he makes there will not -- could be used in any of the meetings, in any future trial and court procedures in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I will report that we were not conducting an investigation, we're just gathering information.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that Johan Tarculovski was not warned that his statement will be used in any procedure in -- in a disciplinary procedure against him or any other person?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You did not warn him that those statements could be used in an administrative procedure against him or another person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: Apart from informing him of the right for attorney, no other rights were told -- we did not tell Mr. Tarculovski of any other rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that according to the Law on Criminal Procedure in the Republic of Macedonia that is any statements given in a police station in front of the police cannot be used in the court procedure afterwards?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not work in that area. But from what I hear, I think that is true. But I do not work in this field.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that you did not warn him about the rights that -- from -- that -- that are important from Article 3, 4, and 210 from the Law on Criminal Procedure and for which rights you are responsible to inform him?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not inform anybody of their rights nor were -- had they been warned about this Article that you just read.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it true that the committee did not use the provisions from the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The committee was established -- I don't want to speak without having that in front of me, but there are certain provisions according to which the committee was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that you did not use the Law on Criminal Procedure in the course of this procedure in the work of this committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were -- we did not conduct an investigation to implement these provisions. This was just an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that in the course of the work the committee did not use the provisions from the administrative procedure of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give you the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that in the work -- during the work, the committee did not abide by the disciplinary procedure within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had not identified any kind of responsibility in order to start the disciplinary procedure and it is not our authority to do so. There is a separate committee that recognises and identifies somebody's disciplinary responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Article 156 of the Law on Criminal Procedure. That is P number 88, exhibit 88, N001-9063, Macedonian version, and N001-9177-037, English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask the speakers to pause between question and answer. There is interpretation going on in several languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is it Article 156. Do you see it on the display in front of you?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that in Article 156 it says that in the undertaking of investigative activity, the Ministry of Interior acts according to the relevant provisions for the Law on Investigative Activities?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that -- does that mean in the course of the work and in the conducting of any kind of activities, the Ministry of the Interior needs to abide by the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true, and we had the opportunity to see yesterday the summons that you gave -- gave to Mr. Johan Tarculovski, since you said that you have issued summons to all civilians, that it is -- that the summons were issued according to the Law on Criminal Procedure, because on the receipt it says that -- that the party was warned according to the provisions of certain Article 156 that if the person does not show up voluntarily that person will taken in by force?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question, because the issuing of the summons and the whole procedure was realised by other members of the committee, so I cannot answer anything about this part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to -- that the witness be shown 56 TR, 6285 -- 2885.8 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would like to ask again the speakers to pause between question and answer for the interpretation and for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter -- it's in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You can see the receipt in front of you. That is the same receipt that my colleagues from the Prosecution showed you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that here we can see at the last paragraph just above the signatures, that it says: "I was warned of the consequences pursuant to Article 142, paragraph 3 of the Law on Criminal Procedure."

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this mean that the committee invited people to -- to an interview according to the provisions of the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really give you an answer on this because the instruction that this be issued and the way in this receipts were issued were done by other members of the committee. This document was given to me in order to include it in the file so as to prove that this person was invited according to the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But as a colleague, a lawyer, can you confirm to me that this receipt is -- has the legal part, caution according to the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this mean that you had to work according to the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the introduction of the decision -- the introduction to the decision lists our task and what is it that we have to do. I clarify that we were on the working on the part concerning the collecting of the information for the purpose of finding, determining what is it that was happening in the village of Ljuboten. And we did not undertake any other activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since you are a MOI employee with a long career, could you answer me this: Is it true that on the basis of the information gathered, the MOI compiles a criminal report where it indicates the evidence that they have learned or obtained?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I work in the analytics department for 15 years, but I have seen a criminal report in the course of my work, and as a lawyer I can say that it contains facts and evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So my conclusion is correct, that the MOI compiles the criminal report where it indicates the evidence that it has found and it submits this to the public prosecutor's office, basic public prosecutor's office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the criminal report does not contain the contents of the statements that certain citizens have given in the course of information gathering?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that our colleagues do not enclose the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is provided in Article 142, paragraph 6 of the Law on Criminal Procedure for the purposes of the transcript. And this is Exhibit P88. Is it so, because the court could not use the statements given to the police as evidence, that is pursuant to Article 149 of the Law on criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the Article number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown ERN N001-9177-019, English version, and ERN N001-9039, Macedonian version, Exhibit P88.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the Article 79 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this refresh your memory, in relation to the previous question I've asked you?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that since the court cannot use statements given to the police as evidence, they are not entered into the criminal report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer again. I think so, from what I've seen of criminal reports, considering that I do not produce criminal reports. But from what I have seen, these statements are not enclosed as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I have asked you before what was the quorum, the minimum number of attendees necessary for the committee to work? Could you tell me considering that the committee had seven members, what was the majority with which the committee made its decisions?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a quorum pre-determined or any majority since the only decisions adopted by the committee were the decisions related which persons -- related to which persons to invite for interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, you had produced several reports. Was it necessary for all committee members to be in agreement so that the reports are initialed and developed?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have clarified the procedure. After I would draft the information, I would submit it to the members who were in attendance. When I receive agreement in feedback, I then communicated to the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you had no final document on the operation of the committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had final information from which -- information from the final meeting, information from the final meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is the information dated 25th of November, 2003?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the committee did not fulfil the tasks for which it was established?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not answer this, because the -- it was planned for the committee to meet one more time, and all members of the committee were supposed to take a joint position regarding all the tasks that were set forth in the decision for the establishment of the committee. So regarding each of the items in the decision, a joint position of the committee should have been established and written, because a valid document is only that which is signed by all committee members.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the committee did not establish the capacity and the number of members of the unit which was active in Ljuboten in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say it again. We had no meeting where we would all sit down, where all members of the committee would review all tasks set forth in the decision from the first one until the last one and then indicate what actions have we take and what we had ascertained.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that the committee failed to complete the task for which it was established. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The committee ask not produce a final report where it would present the results of its work.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness, so I will give the time to my learned friend from the Prosecution as it was agreed between us before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, today at page 37 of the transcript, you were asked about an Official Note by Mr. Tarculovski referenced in the 6th of May, 2003 report. Can I ask you: What was the purpose of having these persons who were interviewed by the commission prepare Official Notes?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the Official Note is to have a record, that the person has been in attendance before the committee and to make record of the statement that the person gave.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So were these Official Notes, in particular the ones that we looked at yesterday, were these Official Notes attached to the informations that were eventually submitted to the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And why -- why not?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the minister of the interior is informed through the information, the document entitled information. That information contains the data on the interviews that were held. The additional documents are never attached to the information. The documents on the basis of which the information is produced are never attached to the actual information.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. You were also asked today about a fact - this is it page 40 of the transcript - that was not mentioned in the report dated 6th of May, 2003. And I understand this report was generated by your colleague. Would these informations then include the important parts of informations dated to the commission that may not have been included in Official Notes produced by the actual person interviewed?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I was not able to understand your question from the interpretation I heard. Perhaps you should speak a bit more slowly so the interpreters are able to interpret what you are say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My apologies. I will make the question a little bit briefer. That might make it easier. The informations that were produced, did they include just the important parts of these statements obtained by the committee?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So these are not stenographic notes, so that everything is taken verbatim. These are parts of the statements that the colleagues gave in the course of the interviews we had with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And as a note-taker, were there instances where you would take notes based on the statements being made and sometimes those notes did not actually reflect what was indicated in the Official Note produced by the person?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did note discrepancies between what was said and what was presented later in the Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could just please display for the witness an exhibit already admitted as P00088, which was already displayed a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's clarification. In line 79.2, I did notice discrepancies, instead of I did note discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I apologise, it's the page bearing ERN N001-9194 in English. It's N001-9194 in English. It would be page 18. And it should be around page 18 of the Macedonian as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Ms. Groseva, what's appearing on the screen here is some articles from the Code of Criminal Procedure for Macedonia and I would just like to draw your attention to the top there to Article 75, actually, it's in the middle of the Macedonian. Subdivision one says: "For each act in the criminal procedure, a minutes will be constructed at the time when the act is being conducted. And if it is not possible, then immediately after." And then in Article 76, just at the bottom of the Macedonian version. Subdivision two says: "The minutes should contain crucial data on the duration and contents of the initiated act in the minutes in form of reporting only the crucial content of the given statements and announcements are notified." Do you see that, Ms. Groseva?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I apologise. Which article did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was referring to Article 57, initially, and then Article 76 we would have to turn the page in Macedonian. My apologies. The very top. I read to you subdivision two which indicates: "That the minutes should contain crucial data on the duration and the contents of the initiated act in the minutes in form of reporting only the crucial content of the given statements and announcements are notified." Do you now see that, Ms. Groseva?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: These two procedures that are outlined in these two articles, then, are similar to the procedures that your committee actually utilised in generating the information. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that in -- you read well in the previous article that this is criminal procedure. Article 76, 75.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My question was just whether or not the procedures are similar to those utilised by yourself in taking the minutes?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no similarities in the procedures. We were just working on collecting the information. We were not conducting an illegal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The -- I guess, I'm using maybe the wrong word and I'm not saying procedures. What I'm saying is, during your interviews with these persons were the -- were similar minutes taken that I have just read to you like those set forth in Article 76?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know if this particular report dated June -- 6 May 2003, was circulated to others in the commission?

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the first minutes?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 6th of May, 2003, the report generated by your colleague --

utterances.speaker: TATJANA GROSEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At which I was not present. I do not know. I don't know -- I found that minutes in the file on the work of the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a few more questions, and I see the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, regrettably, we must adjourn now. I'm sorry, but it will be necessary, and we will continue at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
